drug_name: Darunavir, Cobicistat, Emtricitabine, and Tenofovir Alafenamide
what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat HIV-1 (Human Immunodeficiency Virus) infection in adults and children who weigh at least 40 kg (about 88 pounds). It helps lower the amount of HIV virus in your blood, which helps keep your immune system healthier and lowers your chances of getting infections or other HIV-related illnesses. This medicine does NOT cure HIV, and you can still pass HIV to others while taking it.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth ONCE a day WITH food. Food helps your body absorb the medicine properly and also helps reduce stomach upset. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, break, or chew it. Try to take it at the same time every day to keep a steady level of medicine in your body. Do not stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel well. Stopping suddenly can make the virus harder to treat.
dosing: The usual dose for adults and children weighing at least 40 kg is ONE tablet taken once daily with food. Each tablet contains darunavir 800 mg, cobicistat 150 mg, emtricitabine 200 mg, and tenofovir alafenamide 10 mg. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions. Do not take more or less than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been LESS than 18 hours since your scheduled dose, take the missed dose with food as soon as you remember, then take your next dose at your regular time. If it has been MORE than 18 hours since your scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and just take your next dose at the regular time. NEVER take two doses at the same time or double up to make up for a missed dose. If you are unsure what to do, call your pharmacist or doctor.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in the original bottle with the lid tightly closed. Keep this medicine away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture — do NOT store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. If you have unused medicine, ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it safely.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking other medicines without first checking with your doctor or pharmacist, because this medicine can interact with MANY other drugs, including: certain cholesterol medications (like simvastatin or lovastatin), some seizure medicines (like carbamazepine or phenytoin), certain antibiotics and antifungals, some heartburn and ulcer medicines, blood thinners, and herbal supplements like St. John's Wort — which can make this medicine less effective. Avoid drinking too much alcohol. Do not share needles, syringes, or personal items that may have blood on them. Always use protection (such as condoms) during sexual activity to reduce the risk of spreading HIV.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or get emergency help if you notice any of the following: signs of a serious allergic reaction (rash, fever, blistering or peeling skin, mouth sores, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, trouble breathing); signs of liver problems (yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark or tea-colored urine, pale stools, severe stomach pain, loss of appetite, nausea or vomiting); signs of kidney problems (decreased urination, swelling in legs or ankles, unusual tiredness); severe stomach pain that may spread to your back (possible sign of lactic acidosis or pancreatitis); bone pain or fractures; signs of immune system recovery reactions such as new infections or inflammation; mood changes, depression, or thoughts of self-harm; or any new or worsening symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: This medicine starts working right away to lower the HIV virus levels in your blood, but you will NOT feel any different at first. It usually takes several weeks to months to see the full benefit, such as improved immune cell counts (CD4 counts) and undetectable viral loads. It is very important to keep taking this medicine every day as prescribed — even when you feel healthy — because the virus can come back quickly if you stop or skip doses. Regular blood tests will show how well the medicine is working.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant, plan to become pregnant, or become pregnant while taking this medicine. Your doctor will discuss the risks and benefits. There is a pregnancy registry available to monitor outcomes — ask your doctor or pharmacist for details. BREASTFEEDING: Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine. HIV can be passed to your baby through breast milk. KIDNEY DISEASE: This medicine is NOT recommended for patients with severe kidney disease (creatinine clearance less than 30 mL/min). Your doctor will monitor your kidney function with regular blood and urine tests while you are on this medicine. LIVER DISEASE: Use with caution if you have liver problems. This medicine is NOT recommended for patients with severe liver disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had hepatitis B or C. OLDER ADULTS: Older adults may be more sensitive to the effects of this medicine, especially kidney and bone effects. Regular monitoring is recommended. CHILDREN: This medicine is approved for children who weigh at least 40 kg (about 88 pounds). Safety and effectiveness in children under this weight has not been established.
